profile: Listed on the 2010 Hurun China Rich List (approx. US$150m) with wealth from Tongju Group (mining, hotels). Web searches in English and Chinese (王宝珍 / 同聚集团) returned no verifiable information on this person or the group.

name: Atit Agarwal
current_role: Former Non-Executive Chairman, Responsive Industries Ltd (Mumbai) - chairmanship ended 2018; current role not confirmed
profile: Atit Omprakash Agarwal is a member of the Agarwal family that owns and manages Responsive Industries, a BSE/NSE-listed Mumbai maker of PVC/vinyl, SPC and LVT flooring, synthetic leather and (via Axiom Cordages) ropes. He chaired the company until 2018; the family business has since been fronted by Rishabh Agarwal.
interesting_fact: Responsive Industries describes itself as India's No.1 LVP/SPC flooring maker, with plants in India, Vietnam and Thailand exporting to 70+ countries; the family moved from ropes into PVC flooring in the early 1990s.
notes: Low public profile; little press coverage of Atit personally. Insider profiles (MarketScreener) show chairmanship ending 2018-09-30. Company contacts are corporate, not personal. Best route probably via company office or Rishabh Agarwal.

name: Sat Paul Singhla
current_role: Founder & Managing Director, S P Singla Constructions / SPS Construction India Pvt Ltd
profile: Sat Paul Singla (also spelled Singhla) is a civil engineer and first-generation entrepreneur who founded S P Singla Constructions in 1996 with no capital. The privately held firm specialises in river bridges, highways and metro work across ~15 Indian states and reported revenue of Rs 1,150 crore in FY2017, while remaining fully owned by him.
interesting_fact: His company built what it calls India's longest cable-stayed bridge, between Okha and Beyt Dwarka in Gujarat, plus an extradosed bridge across the Ganges between Aunta and Simaria in Bihar.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting out on his own he spent 12 years with small construction firms in Punjab and Haryana building river bridges in J&K, Punjab and Himachal; his first project as an entrepreneur was a small bridge over the Yamuna in 1996 worth just Rs 10 lakh.
notes: Private company, low media profile; Forbes India 'Built To Last' profile is the main press source. Registered office New Delhi, corporate office Panchkula (Haryana). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Guan Guoliang
current_role: No current public role found (former chairman of New China Life Insurance)
profile: Guan Guoliang (关国亮) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2007-2008 linked to Orient Group (东方集团; finance, building-materials retail, ports). The best-known person of this name was chairman of New China Life Insurance, a company in which Orient Group was a shareholder, until he resigned in 2007.
notes: Sensitive: Guan resigned as New China Life chairman in 2007 during a regulatory investigation into misuse of company funds (https://chinadigitaltimes.net/?p=10532; https://www.caixinglobal.com/2007-05-30/rhythm-turns-to-ruin-for-insurance-boss-101972182.html). Orient Group (600811.SH) itself faced a CSRC fraud finding in 2025. No recent public info or contacts; not recommended for outreach.

name: Samit Satish Mehta
current_role: Executive Director (Operations), Emcure Pharmaceuticals; Whole-Time Director & CEO, Gennova Biopharmaceuticals
profile: Samit Mehta is the son of Emcure founder Satish Mehta and a whole-time director of the Pune-based drugmaker, which listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. He built Emcure's business in regulated markets (US, EU, Canada) and in July 2026 was named to lead Gennova, its now wholly owned biologics/mRNA subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Gennova developed India's first mRNA COVID-19 vaccine (HGCO19), designed to be stable at 2-8 degrees C; Mehta argued emerging markets would not adopt a vaccine needing a sub-zero cold chain.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a strategy management consultant at Ernst & Young in India.
notes: Gennova also works on saRNA vaccines (e.g. Nipah) - good biotech/manufacturing angle. Emcure's site blocks automated fetches; IR email taken from earnings-call transcript.

name: Jennifer Lawrence
current_role: Actor; co-founder of production company Excellent Cadaver
profile: Oscar-winning American actor (Silver Linings Playbook) from Louisville, Kentucky, best known for The Hunger Games and X-Men films. Her wealth comes from acting fees; since 2018 she has produced through Excellent Cadaver with partner Justine Ciarrocchi (Causeway, No Hard Feelings, Die My Love, 2025).
interesting_fact: In 2025 she received the San Sebastian festival's Donostia Award, becoming its youngest-ever recipient; Martin Scorsese sent her company the novel behind Die My Love and is re-teaming with her on What Happens at Night.
deep_cut_fact: She left school at 14 and calls herself 'self-educated'; between early acting jobs she worked as an assistant nurse at the children's summer camp her mother managed in Kentucky.
notes: Not a business founder in the energy/data-center sense; wealth is entertainment income. No personal social media. Board member of anti-corruption nonprofit RepresentUs; Jennifer Lawrence Foundation funded a cardiac ICU at Kosair Children's Hospital (2016). Any approach would go via her talent agency/publicist (not found published here) or Excellent Cadaver. Low fit for podcast.

name: Mark Newcomer
current_role: President, CEO & Co-founder, Paysign, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAYS), Henderson, Nevada
profile: Mark Newcomer co-founded Paysign (formerly 3PEA) in 2001 and has run it since, taking it from an early prepaid-card issuer processor to a NASDAQ-listed (2018) payments and software platform. It leads U.S. plasma-donor compensation cards and pharma co-pay programs, and in 2025 expanded into SaaS for the blood/plasma industry (Apherion).
interesting_fact: Under Newcomer, Paysign built a market-leading position paying U.S. plasma donors via prepaid cards, then bought software that became the Apherion donor-management ecosystem for blood and plasma centers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied bioscience at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, a background he credits for his interest in platforms for complex, regulated healthcare markets.
notes: Stepped down as chairman in 2025 (Dan Henry became chair), remains CEO. Fintech/healthcare angle rather than energy. Press releases also list ir@paysign.com.

name: Patricia K Poppe
profile: Patti Poppe, a Purdue industrial engineer, spent ~15 years at General Motors (rising to director of operations at Grand River Assembly) before moving to DTE Energy in 2005 and Consumers Energy in 2011, becoming its CEO. Since 2021 she has led PG&E, California's largest utility, through its post-bankruptcy wildfire-safety and grid buildout, including data-center load growth.
interesting_fact: She is described as the first woman to be CEO of two Fortune 500 companies (CMS Energy/Consumers Energy and PG&E).
deep_cut_fact: At GM she turned down a promotion that came with a company car to become a second-shift trim-shop supervisor, which she calls the second-hardest job she's had: 'Take the tough jobs where you're going to learn the core business.'
notes: Excellent fit for energy/data-center podcast (PG&E has a large data-center interconnection queue). Business Roundtable member; inducted into Automotive Hall of Fame. Media relations line published on PG&E pages: 415-973-5930. Approach via PG&E corporate communications.
